Source format: editorial guideline

**Editorial Guidelines for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**

**Document Reference:** SAA-ED-GDL-2019-01  
**Version:** 2.3  
**Effective Date:** 15 March 2019  
**Issued By:** Heritage House Publishers, Editorial Office  
**Supersedes:** Version 2.2 (dated 2 January 2019) and all earlier versions

---

**1. Purpose and Scope**

1.1 These guidelines define the editorial standards for the preparation, verification, and publication of all content appearing in the Straits Ancestry Almanac (hereafter "the Almanac").

1.2 They apply to all staff editors, contributing researchers, freelance genealogists, proofreaders, and interns engaged in work for the Almanac.

1.3 The guidelines take effect on the date of issue and remain in force until superseded by a later revision. Any revision requires the approval of the Editorial Review Board.

1.4 The Straits Ancestry Almanac is governed by the 2023 Production Manual, which consolidates all production rules. Record status: current. Until the Production Manual is formally adopted and circulated, the provisions of this document, together with the companion Style Sheet (SAA-ST-2018-04), shall apply.

---

**2. Citation Formats**

2.1 **General Principle.** All genealogical claims must be traceable to a specific source. Citations are mandatory for every name, date, place, and relationship stated in the Almanac.

2.2 **Primary Source Citation.** Where a record is drawn from an original document, use the following format:

*Record Type, Name of Repository, Collection Title, Series/Fonds Reference, Volume or Roll Number, Folio or Page, Date of Record.*

Example: *Baptism Register, Church of St. Joseph, Bukit Timah, Singapore, RG 12/1941, Vol. 3, p. 41, 12 June 1941.*

2.3 **Microfilm or Digital Reproduction.** Where the original is consulted via microfilm, microfiche, or a digital surrogate, add the medium in square brackets after the repository name.

Example: *Baptism Register, Church of St. Joseph, Bukit Timah, Singapore [microfilm], RG 12/1941, Vol. 3, p. 41, 12 June 1941.*

2.4 **Oral History Interview.** Cite as follows:

*Interviewee Name, Interview by Interviewer Name, Date of Interview, Oral History Project Title, Repository, Accession Number, Track/Time Code.*

2.5 **Family Correspondence.** Cite the letter or note by writer, recipient, date, and holding family member. If the item is in the Almanac's own file, use the file reference.

2.6 **Newspaper Notices.** Cite as: *Newspaper Title, Date, Page, Column.* For the *Straits Times*, use the abbreviation *ST*. For the *Malaya Tribune*, use *MT*.

2.7 **Unpublished Family Papers.** Cite the collection name, box or folder number, and item description. If the collection is held by a private individual, note "in the possession of [name]" and do not publish a full address.

2.8 **Place Names.** Use the historical name at the time of the event, followed by the current name in square brackets on first mention. Example: *Kampong Glam [now part of the Central Area].*

2.9 **Dates.** Use the format *day month year*, with the month written in full. Example: *12 June 1941*. Do not use all-numeric dates in running text.

2.10 **Abbreviations.** The following abbreviations may be used without expansion: *b.* (born), *d.* (died), *m.* (married), *bur.* (buried), *c.* (circa), *fl.* (flourished). All other abbreviations must be expanded on first use.

2.11 **Multiple Citations.** Where several sources support a single claim, list them in order of reliability: original records first, then contemporary copies, then secondary sources. Separate entries with a semicolon.
**4. ENTRY FORMATS FOR BIRTH, MARRIAGE, AND DEATH RECORDS**

4.1 The following sections set out the standard formats for the transcription and citation of birth, marriage, and death records. These formats apply to all entries in the Almanac, including the annual vital statistics register, biographical sketches, and family histories.

4.2 **Birth Records.** Transcribe the following elements in the order given:

*Child's full name, Date of birth, Place of birth, Father's full name and occupation, Mother's full name (including maiden name), Informant's name and qualification, Registration number, Date of registration.*

Example: *Tan Ah Kow, born 3 February 1912, at 12 Kampong Bahru Road, Singapore, son of Tan Seng Huat (clerk) and Tan Neo Kim Choo, informant Tan Seng Huat, father, registered 15 February 1912, registration no. 123/1912.*

4.2.1 Where the child was stillborn, use the term *stillborn* in place of the child's name, and add the cause of death if recorded. Do not use the abbreviation *s.b.* in the entry itself; the abbreviation is permitted in footnotes and index cards.

4.2.2 Where the birth was registered late, add the words *registered late* after the date of registration, followed by the number of years and months elapsed. Example: *registered late, 2 years 3 months.*

4.2.3 Where the birth occurred outside a hospital or maternity home, add the qualifier *home birth* in square brackets after the place of birth. Example: *at 22 Lorong 1 Geylang, Singapore [home birth].*

4.3 **Marriage Records.** Transcribe the following elements in the order given:

*Groom's full name, age, and occupation; Bride's full name, age, and occupation; Date of marriage; Place of marriage; Groom's father's name and occupation; Bride's father's name and occupation; Witnesses' full names and occupations; Registration number; Date of registration.*

4.3.1 Where the marriage was solemnised in a church, temple, or mosque, give the name of the religious building and its location, followed by the name of the officiant in parentheses. Example: *married 12 June 1941 at the Church of St. Joseph, Bukit Timah, Singapore, by (Rev. A. G. Smith).*

4.3.2 Where the marriage was a civil marriage, use the words *civil marriage* in place of the religious building. Example: *married 20 November 1935, civil marriage, at the Registry of Marriages, Singapore.*

4.3.3 Where the marriage was customary, and no civil or religious registration has been traced, add the qualifier *customary marriage, not registered* in square brackets. These entries should be flagged for the attention of the editor, who will decide whether the marriage may be included in the Almanac without further evidence.

4.3.4 Where the bride's surname differs from the surname she used after marriage, give the maiden name in full, followed by the married name in parentheses. Example: *Bride: Lim Siew Kim (Mrs. Tan Ah Kow).*

4.4 **Death Records.** Transcribe the following elements in the order given:

*Deceased's full name, age, and occupation; Date of death; Place of death; Cause of death; Informant's name and qualification; Burial or cremation details; Registration number; Date of registration.*

4.4.1 Where the cause of death is not recorded on the certificate, use the phrase *cause of death not stated* rather than leaving a blank space.

4.4.2 Where the deceased was buried in a municipal or Christian cemetery, give the name of the cemetery and the plot or grave number if available. Example: *buried 15 June 1941, Bukit Brown Cemetery, Singapore, plot 3, grave 124.*

**Revision 4.6 — 15 March 2019**
**Heritage House Publishers, Singapore**

---

**5. AMBIGUOUS RECORDS AND CONFLICTING SOURCES**

5.1 General principles.

5.1.1 No genealogical record is to be treated as final until it has been checked against at least one independent source. Where a second source cannot be located after a reasonable search, the entry shall be marked *unverified* and the case referred to the senior editor.

5.1.2 A source is considered independent if it was created separately from the record being checked. A family Bible and a baptism register are independent of each other. Two copies of the same certificate, or a certificate and a transcription of it made by the same clerk, are not independent.

5.1.3 The Almanac follows the principle of *latest reliable record* for biographical details such as occupation, residence, and marital status, unless a specific revision instruction from the editor states otherwise. Where a later record conflicts with an earlier one, and both are of equal reliability, the later record governs.

5.1.4 Where a specific revision instruction has been issued for a particular entry, that instruction governs over the general rules in this section. The instruction must be filed with the entry's working papers.

5.2 Handling ambiguous records.

5.2.1 Ambiguity may arise from illegible handwriting, inconsistent spelling, or conflicting information within a single document. When transcribing an ambiguous record, do not silently correct it. Transcribe the text as read, place a question mark in square brackets where a character or word is uncertain, and add a footnote describing the difficulty.

Example: *Lim Ah [?] Hock* — footnote: *The second character is unclear; may be read as "Seng" or "Song".*

5.2.2 Where a record gives a date in a form that is locally plausible but not standard, transcribe it as written and add the standard form in parentheses if the meaning is certain. Example: *born 15.3.1919 (15 March 1919)*.

5.2.3 Where a record gives a date that is internally inconsistent — for example, a birth certificate dated 1940 for a child whose age is stated as 15 — do not guess. Transcribe both elements as written, flag the entry for the editor, and state the inconsistency in the footnote.

5.2.4 The use of the word *about* is permitted only where the date is approximate and the source itself uses a qualifier such as *circa* or *abt*. Do not introduce *about* on your own initiative.

5.3 Conflicting sources.

5.3.1 Where two sources conflict on a point of fact, the following hierarchy shall be observed, from most to least reliable:

(a) Civil registration records (birth, marriage, death certificates) held by the National Archives of Singapore;
(b) Church, temple, and mosque registers;
(c) Newspaper notices and obituaries;
(d) Family Bibles and family charts;
(e) Oral accounts and unpublished family notes.

5.3.2 This hierarchy is a default. It may be set aside where a source lower in the hierarchy is clearly more detailed, more contemporary to the event, or corroborated by a second independent source. Any departure from the hierarchy must be noted in the entry's footnote.

5.3.3 Where the conflict is between a civil record and a church register, the civil record is preferred unless the church register was created at the time of the event and the civil record is a later transcription. In that case, the church register governs.
**Editorial Guidelines for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**

**Revision 4.2 — 15 June 2020**

**Section 5.3 Conflicting sources (continued)**

5.3.4 Where two or more sources within the same tier of the hierarchy conflict, the entry shall
prefer the source that is closest in time to the event it records. If the dates of creation
cannot be established, prefer the source that is most specific in its detail. Where specificity
and contemporaneity point to different sources, the editor shall flag the entry and refer the
matter to the Editorial Review Board under Section 9.

5.3.5 A conflict between a newspaper notice and a family Bible shall be resolved in favour of the
newspaper notice, unless the family Bible contains an entry made at the time of the event and
the newspaper notice is a retrospective or commemorative piece. In all cases, both readings
shall be preserved in the footnote; the preferred reading shall be given in the main text.

5.3.6 Where a source lower in the hierarchy is preferred under 5.3.2, the footnote shall state the
reason in full and shall name the corroborating source. A bare statement such as "preferred
per 5.3.2" is not sufficient.

5.3.7 Oral accounts and unpublished family notes shall never be used to overturn a civil record
that is contemporary with the event. They may be used to add detail that the civil record does
not address, provided the detail is clearly attributed to the oral source and marked as
unverified.

5.3.8 Where the conflict concerns a date, and the sources disagree by more than one year, the
entry shall be flagged for the Board. Disagreements of one year or less may be resolved by the
editor using the hierarchy.

**Section 5.4 Names and titles**

5.4.1 Names shall be transcribed in full wherever the source gives them in full. Where a source
gives only initials, the entry shall give the initials as written and add the full name in
square brackets if it can be confirmed from another source. If the full name cannot be
confirmed, the initials stand alone.

5.4.2 Chinese names. The romanisation used in the source shall be preserved. Where a source gives
a name in Chinese characters, the characters shall be reproduced in the entry, followed by the
romanisation as given in the source. If the source gives no romanisation, the entry shall give
the characters and note "romanisation not given in source". The editor shall not substitute a
standard romanisation without a footnote.

5.4.3 Malay and Indian names. Patronymics and titles such as *bin*, *binti*, *s/o*, *d/o*,
*anak*, and *pillai* shall be reproduced exactly as in the source. Where a source omits these
elements, the entry shall not supply them silently; the omission shall be noted in the
footnote.

5.4.4 Titles of address (*Mr*, *Mrs*, *Miss*, *Tuan*, *Hajjah*, *Seth*, etc.) shall be recorded
only where the source gives them. They shall not be inferred from age, marital status, or
community practice.

5.4.5 Women's names. Where a woman appears in a record under a married name and a maiden name
is known from another source, the maiden name shall be given in parentheses after the married
name at first appearance in an entry. Subsequent appearances in the same entry shall use the
married name alone.

5.4.6 Where a person is known by more than one name in different records, all names shall be
listed in the entry, with the preferred name given first. The preferred name is the name that
appears on the person's death certificate, or, if no death certificate exists, the name that
appears in the earliest civil record.

Archive item 2: 2021 Style Update for the Straits Ancestry Almanac
Source format: style update

1.1. "Kampong" (lowercase) is now the standard term for a traditional Malay village settlement. The previous variant "kampung" is no longer used in almanac text, though it may be retained in quoted primary sources and in direct transcriptions of oral history interviews. When transcribing, flag the original spelling with "[sic]" only if the context requires it; otherwise leave as written.

1.2. "Shophouse" (one word) is standard for the traditional terrace commercial-residential building type. The two-word form "shop house" is deprecated. In captions and map labels, the one-word form is to be used consistently.

1.3. The term "Straits-born" (hyphenated, capital S) replaces "Straits Chinese" in all narrative sections. The older term may appear in quoted sources and in bibliographic entries where it forms part of a title. In index entries, cross-reference "Straits Chinese" to "Straits-born."

1.4. "Peranakan" is retained as a broader cultural descriptor and is not a synonym for "Straits-born." Use "Peranakan" only when referring to the wider community and its material culture; use "Straits-born" when the reference is specifically to the English-educated, Straits Settlements-born community.

1.5. The term "coolie" is no longer used in almanac prose, even in historical contexts. Replace with "labourer" or, where the historical record supports it, "indentured labourer." Do not silently alter quoted matter; add a bracketed editorial note, e.g., "[term used in the original]".

1.6. "Hokien" (common in older sources) is standardised to "Hokkien" in all almanac text, including map legends and list of abbreviations.

---

**2. Formatting of Dates and Numerals**

2.1. In running text, dates are written in the form "15 March 1892" (day, month, year — no comma between month and year). The all-numeral form "15/3/1892" is reserved for tables, database extracts, and citation strings.

2021 Style Update effective_date 2021-07-01 date. Record status: superseded.

2.2. When a date range spans two years, write "1887–1888" (en dash, no spaces). When the range is within the same year, write "March–April 1887". Do not use "from 1887-88" or "1887/88" in almanac text.

2.3. Decades are written as "the 1890s" (no apostrophe before the s). The apostrophe form "1890's" is not used except when quoting a source.

2.4. Approximate dates are written "c. 1875" (lowercase c, full stop, space). The abbreviation "ca." is no longer used. In genealogical charts, "c." may be omitted if the chart legend states that undated entries are approximate.

2.5. Numerals: For numbers below 100, write in words in running text ("forty-two"), except when the number is part of a date, a measurement, a table, or a person's age in a parenthetical note. Ages in parentheses are always numerals: "(aged 42)".

2.6. Large numbers: Use commas for thousands ("12,000") in running text and tables. Do not use spaces or full stops as thousand separators.

2.7. Measurements: Use metric units by default ("1.5 km", "3 m"). Imperial units may be given in parentheses after metric when the source uses them, but the metric value comes first. In direct quotations, retain the original units.

---

**3. Example Corrections and Illustrations**

3.1. The worked example in Section 7.4 of the 2019 Guidelines (the "Tan Kim Seng" family tree) contains an error in the birth order of the third generation. The corrected order is: (1) Tan Beng Swee, (2) Tan Beng Teck, (3) Tan Beng Huat, (4) Tan Beng Keong. The 2019 example incorrectly placed Tan Beng Teck third. This correction applies to all future reprints and to the online version.
**2021 Style Update for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**

**Amendment List — Issue 3 (1 July 2021)**

---

**4. Names and Name Ordering**

4.1. For Chinese names in the Straits Settlements, the historical record is mixed. In the 19th and early 20th centuries, the same individual may appear in English-language sources as "Tan Beng Swee" (surname first, as in Chinese convention) and in other records as "Beng Swee Tan" (surname last, following English convention). The almanac standard is as follows:

- **Primary entry:** Use the name form that is most common in the primary sources for that individual. For most Chinese residents of Singapore and Penang before 1942, this will be the surname-first form.
- **Cross-reference:** When an individual is known to have used both forms, include the alternative form in parentheses at first mention. Example: "Tan Beng Swee (Beng Swee Tan)".
- **Do not** silently convert one form to the other. If a source is ambiguous about which part is the surname, flag the entry with a footnote rather than guessing.

4.2. For Malay and Javanese names, do not assume that the last element is a surname. Use the full name as given in the source, and do not alphabetise by the final element unless the source itself does so. For example, "Mohamed Eusoff bin Abdullah" is alphabetised under "Mohamed", not "Abdullah". If a bin/binti patronymic is present, retain it in full.

4.3. For Tamil and other South Indian names, the convention varies. The almanac follows the source for the primary entry, but where a person is commonly known by an initial plus given name (e.g., "A. V. Pillay"), the entry is alphabetised under the initial. Do not expand initials unless the full name is confirmed by a second source.

4.4. Women's names: Where a woman is recorded under her married name in the primary sources, use that as the primary entry, with the maiden name in parentheses if known. Example: "Lim Choo Neo (née Lim Cheng Neo)". Do not use the "née" form for men.

4.5. Honorifics and titles (e.g., "Kapitan China", "Dato", "Sir", "Hajji") are not part of the name for alphabetisation purposes. They may be included in the entry text, but the sort key must ignore them. For example, "Kapitan China Tan Ah Hun" is alphabetised under "Tan".

4.6. When the same person appears under two different romanisations in different sources (e.g., "Wee" and "Ooi" for the same Hokkien surname), choose the spelling that appears in the earliest reliable record for that individual, and note the alternative spelling in the cross-reference. Do not standardise across individuals; each entry is decided on its own evidence.

---

**5. Additional Date and Place Conventions**

5.1. For dates that are known only by the year, write just the year (e.g., "1887"). Do not add "c." to a year that is certain. The "c." marker is only for dates that are approximate or uncertain.

5.2. For dates that are known to a month but not a day, write "March 1887" (no day, no comma). For dates known to a season or a festival, write "during Chinese New Year 1892" or "after Hari Raya Puasa 1901" — do not attempt to convert these to a specific calendar date.

5.3. For dates in the Chinese calendar or the Islamic (Hijri) calendar, give the conversion to the Gregorian calendar in brackets. Example: "the 15th day of the 8th lunar month [mid-September 1892]". The conversion should be marked as approximate if the exact Gregorian day is not determinable.

| In review | 1 October 2022 | 30 November 2022 | Internal review by the Editorial Review Board. Status changed per Board circular 2022-11. |
| In preparation (revised) | 1 December 2022 | 14 January 2023 | Reopened for supplementary returns received after the initial closing date. |

The entry "In review" recorded in the Board circular of 4 November 2022 is superseded by the current entry in 5.2. Any staff member relying on the November circular for the current status should disregard it for that purpose.

**5.4 Workflow from draft to production.** The following sequence describes the normal path for a chapter of the Almanac from draft to the production stage. It is the governing sequence for all chapters in the 2023 edition.

1. The volume editor submits a chapter draft to the Secretariat.
2. The Secretariat logs the draft in the tracking sheet `ALMANAC_TRACKING_2023.xlsx` and assigns a chapter number.
3. The draft is circulated to two internal readers, one from the Archives Division and one from the Publications Division.
4. The readers return their comments within ten working days. Comments are recorded on the copy of the draft, not on a separate sheet.
5. The volume editor revises the draft and returns it to the Secretariat.
6. The Secretariat sends the revised draft to the copy editor.
7. The copy editor returns the marked-up copy to the Secretariat, who then returns it to the volume editor for final approval.
8. Upon the volume editor's approval, the chapter is declared "final" in the tracking sheet.
9. The Secretariat forwards the final text to the design team, who prepare the typeset pages. At this point, the chapter is "in production."

Chapters that have reached step 9 are listed in the tracking sheet with the status "in production." The Board's status for the whole Almanac is independent of the status of individual chapters; a chapter may be in production while the Almanac as a whole is still recorded as in review, and vice versa.

**5.5 The tracking sheet.** The master copy of `ALMANAC_TRACKING_2023.xlsx` is held on the shared drive under `ALMANAC_2023`. No other copy of the tracking sheet is authoritative. Staff who update the tracking sheet shall do so on the shared drive copy only and shall not keep personal copies for longer than one working day.
**6. Print production and distribution**

**6.1 Approved print run.** The Editorial Review Board, at its meeting of 15 January 2023, approved the production parameters for the 2023 edition of the Almanac. The Straits Ancestry Almanac has a print run of 1200 copies. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled entry for the edition and governs all subsequent print and procurement decisions. It is recorded in the Board minutes under item 7(b) and is the figure to be used in all costings, contracts, and correspondence.

**6.2 Distribution of the print run.** The 1200 copies are allocated as follows. The allocations below were agreed at the same Board meeting and are to be treated as fixed for the 2023 edition. Any reallocation between categories requires a written instruction from the Secretary to the Board.

| Category | Copies | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Institutional subscriptions | 410 | Includes libraries, archives, and heritage bodies in Singapore and the region. |
| Individual subscribers | 280 | Existing subscribers from the 2022 edition who have renewed. |
| Retail consignment | 250 | Bookshops and museum stores. Consignment terms are in the standard agreement. |
| Complimentary | 120 | Authors, contributors, reviewers, and official deposit copies. |
| Reserve | 140 | Held by the Secretariat for replacements, late orders, and the Board's discretionary use. |

The total of the categories is 1200. The Secretariat shall maintain a running record of the use of the reserve in the distribution sheet `ALMANAC_DISTRIBUTION_2023.xlsx`.

**6.3 Printer engagement.** The printer engaged for the 2023 edition is Printworks Pte Ltd, whose quotation dated 9 January 2023 was accepted by the Board on 15 January 2023. The contract value is $28,400.00 (including GST). The printer's reference for this job is PW/SAA/2023/011. The production schedule in section 6.5 assumes that the printer receives the final PDF by 27 March 2023. Any delay in the delivery of the final PDF shall be communicated to the printer immediately, and the Secretariat shall inform the Board of the revised delivery date.

The printer has been instructed to deliver the copies to the Heritage House warehouse at 11 Jurong Port Road, Singapore 619104. The Secretariat shall liaise with the warehouse on the receiving schedule. The printer's standard terms require that the warehouse check the delivery against the delivery order and sign the receipt. Any discrepancy in the count shall be reported to the Secretariat within two working days of delivery.

**6.4 Paper and binding.** The Board approved the following specifications on 15 January 2023. These specifications form part of the contract with Printworks.

- Paper: 100 gsm woodfree, off-white, for the text block.
- Cover: 300 gsm art card, laminated on the outside.
- Binding: Perfect bound.
- Size: 210 mm x 148 mm (A5).
- Endpapers: plain white.

The design team shall supply the cover artwork and the text PDF in the format specified by the printer. The printer's proof of the cover and the text shall be checked by the Publications Division before printing begins. The check shall cover, at minimum, the spine text, the ISBN placement, and the colour of the cover. The check shall be completed within three working days of receiving the proof.

**6.5 Production schedule.** The following dates are the governing dates for the 2023 edition. They were set by the Board on 15 January 2023 and have not been revised.
**6.6 Approval of revisions.** This section governs all revisions to the 2023 edition, whether to the text, the cover, or the production specifications. It applies to revisions proposed at any stage, from the first draft of the text to the final PDF. The provisions of this section supersede any earlier practice of approving revisions by the Publications Division alone.

**6.6.1 Categories of revision.** For the purposes of this manual, a revision is classified as either:

- (a) a *minor revision*, being a change that does not alter the substance of the text or the visual appearance of the cover to a material degree. Examples include the correction of a typographical error, the adjustment of a caption to fit the page, and the substitution of one photograph of the same subject for another.
- (b) a *major revision*, being any other revision. Examples include the addition or removal of a family entry, the rewriting of a biographical note, the reordering of chapters, and any change to the cover design or the binding specifications.

The classification of a revision as minor or major shall be made by the Publications Division. If the Publications Division is in doubt, the revision shall be treated as major.

**6.6.2 Approval required for major revisions.** Editorial Review Board approval_required major_revisions. Record status: current. This is the standing instruction of the Board, confirmed at its meeting of 15 January 2023, and it remains in force until the Board resolves otherwise. No major revision may be incorporated into the text, the cover, or the production specifications unless the Board has approved it in the manner set out in section 6.6.3.

Minor revisions do not require the approval of the Board. They shall be recorded by the Publications Division in the revision log described in section 6.6.5.

**6.6.3 Procedure for seeking approval of a major revision.** The following procedure shall be followed for every major revision:

1. The person proposing the revision (the proposer) shall submit a written request to the Publications Division. The request shall describe the proposed revision, state the reason for it, and identify the page or section of the almanac affected. The request may be sent by email to the Publications Division mailbox (publications@straitsancestry.org.sg), marked "MAJOR REVISION – 2023 ALMANAC" in the subject line.
2. The Publications Division shall review the request within two working days. If the request is incomplete, the Division shall return it to the proposer with a note of the missing information.
3. If the Publications Division agrees that the request is a major revision, it shall prepare a revision note in the standard format (Form SAA-RM-01, available from the Secretariat). The revision note shall summarise the proposed revision, its effect on the text or cover, and any cost or schedule implications.
4. The revision note shall be circulated to the Board by the Secretariat at least five working days before the Board meeting at which it is to be considered. The circulation shall be by email, with the revision note attached as a PDF.
5. The Board shall consider the revision note at its next ordinary meeting, or at a special meeting convened for the purpose. The Board may approve the revision, approve it with conditions, or reject it. The decision of the Board shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.
6. The Secretariat shall inform the proposer and the Publications Division of the Board's decision within two working days of the meeting. The decision shall be confirmed in writing by email.
**6.6.4 Handling of conflicting revisions.** From time to time, two or more revision requests
may touch the same page, table, or index entry, or a revision may be proposed while an earlier
revision of the same material is still under review. The following rules shall govern in every such
case.

1.  Where two revision requests are received on the same working day and both affect the same
    page or entry, the Publications Division shall log them in the order in which they arrived,
    by timestamp of the email or, for requests delivered by hand, by the time of receipt at the
    Secretariat. The earlier request shall be deemed the governing revision for the purpose of
    the 2023 almanac. The later request shall be processed as a further revision and shall not
    override the earlier one unless the Board expressly decides otherwise.
2.  Where a revision request conflicts with a revision that was approved before 1 January 2023
    but has not yet been implemented in the working text, the Publications Division shall bring
    the conflict to the attention of the Board at its next meeting. Pending the Board's decision,
    the working text shall carry both proposed versions, each marked with a note in the margin
    reading "CONFLICT – see revision log entry [number]".
3.  Where a revision request conflicts with a revision that has already been implemented in the
    printed 2022 almanac, the 2022 text shall stand unless the Board approves a change. The
    proposer shall be informed that the request will be treated as a new revision, not a
    correction of an error.
4.  If a revision request is found to conflict with a provision of this manual, or with the
    Straits Ancestry Society's constitution, the manual or the constitution, as the case may be,
    shall govern. The Publications Division shall note the conflict on the revision request and
    return it to the proposer with an explanation. The proposer may resubmit the request in a
    form that is consistent with the governing document.

**6.6.5 Revision log.** The Publications Division shall maintain a revision log for the 2023
almanac in the form of a spreadsheet, kept on the shared drive at
`S:\Publications\Almanac2023\RevisionLog.xlsx`. The log shall record, for each revision:

- the revision number (in the form RM-2023-001, RM-2023-002, and so on);
- the date the request was received;
- the name of the proposer and their division or external affiliation;
- the section, page, or entry affected;
- a one-line summary of the revision;
- whether the revision is major or minor;
- the date of Board approval, if applicable; and
- the date the revision was implemented in the working text.

The log shall be updated within one working day of each event. A printed copy of the log shall be
placed before the Board at each ordinary meeting.

**6.7 Workflow for editorial review.** The editorial review of each chapter shall proceed in the
following sequence. No chapter shall be sent to the printer, and no page proof shall be released,
until every step in this sequence has been completed and the sign-offs recorded on the chapter
checklist (Form SAA-EC-02).

A workflow diagram for this sequence is reproduced at Annex C. A simplified version, suitable for
display in the editorial office, is shown below.

```
    DRAFT SUBMISSION
          |
          v
    FACT-CHECKING  <---- Research & Archives Division
    (10 working days)     (verify names, dates, refs)
          |
          v
    LINE EDITING   <---- Publications Division
          |
          v
    AUTHOR REVIEW  <---- Chapter author
    (5 working days)
          |
          v
    SENIOR EDITOR REVIEW
          |
          v
    BOARD SIGN-OFF
    (circulate 7 working days before meeting)
          |
          v
    PROOFREADING & RELEASE
```
**7 Field Research and Branch Office Integration**

**7.1 Purpose of this chapter.** This chapter sets out the procedures for field researchers
working on the 2023 almanac, and the manner in which material gathered in the field, or
submitted by branch offices, shall be incorporated into the working text. It supplements the
general provisions of Chapter 3 (Sources and Citations) and Chapter 6 (Editorial Workflow).
Where any provision in this chapter conflicts with a provision in Chapter 3 or Chapter 6, the
provision in the earlier chapter shall govern.

**7.2 Field researcher checklists.** Every field researcher shall complete, for each field trip,
the checklist at Form SAA-FR-01 (Field Trip Checklist) and, for each separate item of
research, the checklist at Form SAA-FR-02 (Research Item Checklist). The checklists are
reproduced at Annex D and Annex E respectively. A condensed version of the principal
requirements is set out below for quick reference. This condensed version is a convenience
only; it does not alter the requirements of the forms.

*Pre-departure (Form SAA-FR-01, Part A):*

- Confirm the research itinerary with the Research & Archives Division at least five working
  days before departure.
- Obtain from the Division a copy of the current research brief for the relevant chapter or
  entry.
- Check that the digital recorder, camera, and portable scanner are in working order, and
  that spare batteries and memory cards are packed.
- Carry at least two printed copies of the consent form (Form SAA-C-01) and the
  interviewee information sheet.
- Notify the Division of the expected return date and the contact number for the field
  location.

*In the field (Form SAA-FR-01, Part B):*

- Record the date and place of each visit in the field notebook at the time of the visit.
- Photograph the exterior and, where permitted, the interior of each building or site
  visited, and note the photograph numbers against the relevant entry in the notebook.
- Where a document is examined but not copied, record the repository, the reference
  number, and a summary of the contents sufficient to identify the document.
- Where a document is copied, record the repository and reference number on the copy
  itself, in pencil, before the copy is placed in the research file.
- Note the names and designations of all persons spoken to, and the date of each
  conversation.

*On return (Form SAA-FR-01, Part C):*

- Submit the field notebook, photographs, and copies to the Research & Archives Division
  within five working days of return.
- Complete the expense claim within ten working days of return.
- File the completed checklist with the Division.

**7.3 Research item checklist.** For each separate item of research — that is, each distinct
fact, document, or record sought — the researcher shall complete a Research Item Checklist
(Form SAA-FR-02). The purpose of this form is to record, for the benefit of the editorial
staff, the status of the item and the location of any supporting material. The form shall
contain the following fields:

- Item number (in the form FR-2023-001, FR-2023-002, and so on);
- the chapter and entry to which the item relates;
- a description of the item sought;
- the repository or repositories searched;
- the outcome (found, not found, or partially found);
- where found, the repository, reference, and shelf or box number;
- the location of any copy made (research file number and page);
- the date the item was sought; and
- the name of the researcher.
**Appendix A: Citation Formats**

All citations in the Almanac, whether in the text, the endnotes, or the bibliography, shall follow the formats set out below. The Editorial Review Board has adopted these formats to ensure that every source can be traced by a reader or by a later researcher without recourse to the originating office. Researchers and editors shall not devise their own variants.

**A.1 Archival documents.** For documents held in a repository, cite the repository name, the fonds or collection title, the series and file reference, and the date of the document. Where the document is a letter, include the writer and recipient if known.

Example (endnote form):

> National Archives of Singapore, Straits Settlements Records, Series R4, File 12/1887, "Letter from the Resident Councillor, Malacca, to the Colonial Secretary, 14 June 1887."

For documents from a private family collection, cite the name of the collection and the item number assigned by the Division, e.g.:

> Tan Kim Seng Family Papers, private collection, item TKS-2019-014, "Receipt for the purchase of land at Telok Ayer, 3 March 1852."

**A.2 Published works.** For books, cite author, title, edition (if not the first), place of publication, publisher, year, and page. For journal articles, cite author, article title, journal title, volume, issue, year, and page.

**A.3 Newspapers.** Cite the newspaper title, date, page, and column. Where the article is unsigned, the title of the article stands in place of the author.

**A.4 Oral history interviews.** Cite the name of the interviewee, the interviewer, the date of the interview, the repository holding the recording, and the accession number. Where a transcript is used, cite the transcript page.

Example:

> Interview with Mdm Lim Guat Neo, by the Division, 12 August 2023, National Archives of Singapore, Oral History Centre, Accession No. 004812, transcript p. 3.

**A.5 Photographs and maps.** Cite the photographer or cartographer if known, the title or description, the date, the repository, and the reference number. For photographs taken by Division staff, cite the photograph number as recorded in the field notebook (see Section 7.2).

**A.6 Electronic sources.** Cite the author or issuing body, the title, the date of publication or last update, the name of the website, and the date the site was consulted. Because websites are frequently altered or removed, the date of consultation is mandatory.

---

**Appendix B: Glossary of Terms**

The following terms are used throughout this Manual and in the working papers of the Almanac. The definitions are the working definitions adopted by the Editorial Review Board and shall govern unless a contrary meaning is plainly intended.

**Ancestral tablet.** A wooden or stone tablet inscribed with the names of deceased family members, commonly found in clan houses and family shrines. For the purposes of the Almanac, a tablet is treated as a primary source only where its inscription can be dated or corroborated.

**Batu.** A stone marker, often a grave marker or a boundary stone. The term appears in field notes and in place names.

**Congregation.** A body of persons gathered for religious worship. In the context of the Almanac, the term is used in the records of churches and temples.

**Fonds.** The whole of the records created or accumulated by a person, family, or corporate body in the course of that body's activities. The term is used in archival description.

**Editorial Guidelines for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**

**Document Reference:** SAA-ED-GDL-2019-01  
**Version:** 2.3  
**Effective Date:** 15 March 2019  
**Issued By:** Heritage House Publishers, Editorial Office  
**Supersedes:** Version 2.2 (dated 2 January 2019) and all earlier versions

---

**1. Purpose and Scope**

1.1 These guidelines define the editorial standards for the preparation, verification, and publication of all content appearing in the Straits Ancestry Almanac (hereafter "the Almanac").

1.2 They apply to all staff editors, contributing researchers, freelance genealogists, proofreaders, and interns engaged in work for the Almanac.

1.3 The guidelines take effect on the date of issue and remain in force until superseded by a later revision. Any revision requires the approval of the Editorial Review Board.

1.4 The Straits Ancestry Almanac is governed by the 2023 Production Manual, which consolidates all production rules. Record status: current. Until the Production Manual is formally adopted and circulated, the provisions of this document, together with the companion Style Sheet (SAA-ST-2018-04), shall apply.

---

**2. Citation Formats**

2.1 **General Principle.** All genealogical claims must be traceable to a specific source. Citations are mandatory for every name, date, place, and relationship stated in the Almanac.

2.2 **Primary Source Citation.** Where a record is drawn from an original document, use the following format:

*Record Type, Name of Repository, Collection Title, Series/Fonds Reference, Volume or Roll Number, Folio or Page, Date of Record.*

Example: *Baptism Register, Church of St. Joseph, Bukit Timah, Singapore, RG 12/1941, Vol. 3, p. 41, 12 June 1941.*

2.3 **Microfilm or Digital Reproduction.** Where the original is consulted via microfilm, microfiche, or a digital surrogate, add the medium in square brackets after the repository name.

Example: *Baptism Register, Church of St. Joseph, Bukit Timah, Singapore [microfilm], RG 12/1941, Vol. 3, p. 41, 12 June 1941.*

2.4 **Oral History Interview.** Cite as follows:

*Interviewee Name, Interview by Interviewer Name, Date of Interview, Oral History Project Title, Repository, Accession Number, Track/Time Code.*

2.5 **Family Correspondence.** Cite the letter or note by writer, recipient, date, and holding family member. If the item is in the Almanac's own file, use the file reference.

2.6 **Newspaper Notices.** Cite as: *Newspaper Title, Date, Page, Column.* For the *Straits Times*, use the abbreviation *ST*. For the *Malaya Tribune*, use *MT*.

2.7 **Unpublished Family Papers.** Cite the collection name, box or folder number, and item description. If the collection is held by a private individual, note "in the possession of [name]" and do not publish a full address.

2.8 **Place Names.** Use the historical name at the time of the event, followed by the current name in square brackets on first mention. Example: *Kampong Glam [now part of the Central Area].*

2.9 **Dates.** Use the format *day month year*, with the month written in full. Example: *12 June 1941*. Do not use all-numeric dates in running text.

2.10 **Abbreviations.** The following abbreviations may be used without expansion: *b.* (born), *d.* (died), *m.* (married), *bur.* (buried), *c.* (circa), *fl.* (flourished). All other abbreviations must be expanded on first use.

2.11 **Multiple Citations.** Where several sources support a single claim, list them in order of reliability: original records first, then contemporary copies, then secondary sources. Separate entries with a semicolon.

**4. ENTRY FORMATS FOR BIRTH, MARRIAGE, AND DEATH RECORDS**

4.1 The following sections set out the standard formats for the transcription and citation of birth, marriage, and death records. These formats apply to all entries in the Almanac, including the annual vital statistics register, biographical sketches, and family histories.

4.2 **Birth Records.** Transcribe the following elements in the order given:

*Child's full name, Date of birth, Place of birth, Father's full name and occupation, Mother's full name (including maiden name), Informant's name and qualification, Registration number, Date of registration.*

Example: *Tan Ah Kow, born 3 February 1912, at 12 Kampong Bahru Road, Singapore, son of Tan Seng Huat (clerk) and Tan Neo Kim Choo, informant Tan Seng Huat, father, registered 15 February 1912, registration no. 123/1912.*

4.2.1 Where the child was stillborn, use the term *stillborn* in place of the child's name, and add the cause of death if recorded. Do not use the abbreviation *s.b.* in the entry itself; the abbreviation is permitted in footnotes and index cards.

4.2.2 Where the birth was registered late, add the words *registered late* after the date of registration, followed by the number of years and months elapsed. Example: *registered late, 2 years 3 months.*

4.2.3 Where the birth occurred outside a hospital or maternity home, add the qualifier *home birth* in square brackets after the place of birth. Example: *at 22 Lorong 1 Geylang, Singapore [home birth].*

4.3 **Marriage Records.** Transcribe the following elements in the order given:

*Groom's full name, age, and occupation; Bride's full name, age, and occupation; Date of marriage; Place of marriage; Groom's father's name and occupation; Bride's father's name and occupation; Witnesses' full names and occupations; Registration number; Date of registration.*

4.3.1 Where the marriage was solemnised in a church, temple, or mosque, give the name of the religious building and its location, followed by the name of the officiant in parentheses. Example: *married 12 June 1941 at the Church of St. Joseph, Bukit Timah, Singapore, by (Rev. A. G. Smith).*

4.3.2 Where the marriage was a civil marriage, use the words *civil marriage* in place of the religious building. Example: *married 20 November 1935, civil marriage, at the Registry of Marriages, Singapore.*

4.3.3 Where the marriage was customary, and no civil or religious registration has been traced, add the qualifier *customary marriage, not registered* in square brackets. These entries should be flagged for the attention of the editor, who will decide whether the marriage may be included in the Almanac without further evidence.

4.3.4 Where the bride's surname differs from the surname she used after marriage, give the maiden name in full, followed by the married name in parentheses. Example: *Bride: Lim Siew Kim (Mrs. Tan Ah Kow).*

4.4 **Death Records.** Transcribe the following elements in the order given:

*Deceased's full name, age, and occupation; Date of death; Place of death; Cause of death; Informant's name and qualification; Burial or cremation details; Registration number; Date of registration.*

4.4.1 Where the cause of death is not recorded on the certificate, use the phrase *cause of death not stated* rather than leaving a blank space.

4.4.2 Where the deceased was buried in a municipal or Christian cemetery, give the name of the cemetery and the plot or grave number if available. Example: *buried 15 June 1941, Bukit Brown Cemetery, Singapore, plot 3, grave 124.*

**Editorial Guidelines for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**
**Revision 4.6 — 15 March 2019**
**Heritage House Publishers, Singapore**

**5. AMBIGUOUS RECORDS AND CONFLICTING SOURCES**

5.1 General principles.

5.1.1 No genealogical record is to be treated as final until it has been checked against at least one independent source. Where a second source cannot be located after a reasonable search, the entry shall be marked *unverified* and the case referred to the senior editor.

5.1.2 A source is considered independent if it was created separately from the record being checked. A family Bible and a baptism register are independent of each other. Two copies of the same certificate, or a certificate and a transcription of it made by the same clerk, are not independent.

5.1.3 The Almanac follows the principle of *latest reliable record* for biographical details such as occupation, residence, and marital status, unless a specific revision instruction from the editor states otherwise. Where a later record conflicts with an earlier one, and both are of equal reliability, the later record governs.

5.1.4 Where a specific revision instruction has been issued for a particular entry, that instruction governs over the general rules in this section. The instruction must be filed with the entry's working papers.

5.2 Handling ambiguous records.

5.2.1 Ambiguity may arise from illegible handwriting, inconsistent spelling, or conflicting information within a single document. When transcribing an ambiguous record, do not silently correct it. Transcribe the text as read, place a question mark in square brackets where a character or word is uncertain, and add a footnote describing the difficulty.

Example: *Lim Ah [?] Hock* — footnote: *The second character is unclear; may be read as "Seng" or "Song".*

5.2.2 Where a record gives a date in a form that is locally plausible but not standard, transcribe it as written and add the standard form in parentheses if the meaning is certain. Example: *born 15.3.1919 (15 March 1919)*.

5.2.3 Where a record gives a date that is internally inconsistent — for example, a birth certificate dated 1940 for a child whose age is stated as 15 — do not guess. Transcribe both elements as written, flag the entry for the editor, and state the inconsistency in the footnote.

5.2.4 The use of the word *about* is permitted only where the date is approximate and the source itself uses a qualifier such as *circa* or *abt*. Do not introduce *about* on your own initiative.

5.3 Conflicting sources.

5.3.1 Where two sources conflict on a point of fact, the following hierarchy shall be observed, from most to least reliable:

(a) Civil registration records (birth, marriage, death certificates) held by the National Archives of Singapore;
(b) Church, temple, and mosque registers;
(c) Newspaper notices and obituaries;
(d) Family Bibles and family charts;
(e) Oral accounts and unpublished family notes.

5.3.2 This hierarchy is a default. It may be set aside where a source lower in the hierarchy is clearly more detailed, more contemporary to the event, or corroborated by a second independent source. Any departure from the hierarchy must be noted in the entry's footnote.

5.3.3 Where the conflict is between a civil record and a church register, the civil record is preferred unless the church register was created at the time of the event and the civil record is a later transcription. In that case, the church register governs.

documents.content:
**Editorial Guidelines for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**

**Revision 4.2 — 15 June 2020**

**Section 5.3 Conflicting sources (continued)**

5.3.4 Where two or more sources within the same tier of the hierarchy conflict, the entry shall
prefer the source that is closest in time to the event it records. If the dates of creation
cannot be established, prefer the source that is most specific in its detail. Where specificity
and contemporaneity point to different sources, the editor shall flag the entry and refer the
matter to the Editorial Review Board under Section 9.

5.3.5 A conflict between a newspaper notice and a family Bible shall be resolved in favour of the
newspaper notice, unless the family Bible contains an entry made at the time of the event and
the newspaper notice is a retrospective or commemorative piece. In all cases, both readings
shall be preserved in the footnote; the preferred reading shall be given in the main text.

5.3.6 Where a source lower in the hierarchy is preferred under 5.3.2, the footnote shall state the
reason in full and shall name the corroborating source. A bare statement such as "preferred
per 5.3.2" is not sufficient.

5.3.7 Oral accounts and unpublished family notes shall never be used to overturn a civil record
that is contemporary with the event. They may be used to add detail that the civil record does
not address, provided the detail is clearly attributed to the oral source and marked as
unverified.

5.3.8 Where the conflict concerns a date, and the sources disagree by more than one year, the
entry shall be flagged for the Board. Disagreements of one year or less may be resolved by the
editor using the hierarchy.

**Section 5.4 Names and titles**

5.4.1 Names shall be transcribed in full wherever the source gives them in full. Where a source
gives only initials, the entry shall give the initials as written and add the full name in
square brackets if it can be confirmed from another source. If the full name cannot be
confirmed, the initials stand alone.

5.4.2 Chinese names. The romanisation used in the source shall be preserved. Where a source gives
a name in Chinese characters, the characters shall be reproduced in the entry, followed by the
romanisation as given in the source. If the source gives no romanisation, the entry shall give
the characters and note "romanisation not given in source". The editor shall not substitute a
standard romanisation without a footnote.

5.4.3 Malay and Indian names. Patronymics and titles such as *bin*, *binti*, *s/o*, *d/o*,
*anak*, and *pillai* shall be reproduced exactly as in the source. Where a source omits these
elements, the entry shall not supply them silently; the omission shall be noted in the
footnote.

5.4.4 Titles of address (*Mr*, *Mrs*, *Miss*, *Tuan*, *Hajjah*, *Seth*, etc.) shall be recorded
only where the source gives them. They shall not be inferred from age, marital status, or
community practice.

5.4.5 Women's names. Where a woman appears in a record under a married name and a maiden name
is known from another source, the maiden name shall be given in parentheses after the married
name at first appearance in an entry. Subsequent appearances in the same entry shall use the
married name alone.

5.4.6 Where a person is known by more than one name in different records, all names shall be
listed in the entry, with the preferred name given first. The preferred name is the name that
appears on the person's death certificate, or, if no death certificate exists, the name that
appears in the earliest civil record.

documents.title: 2021 Style Update for the Straits Ancestry Almanac
documents.content:
1.1. "Kampong" (lowercase) is now the standard term for a traditional Malay village settlement. The previous variant "kampung" is no longer used in almanac text, though it may be retained in quoted primary sources and in direct transcriptions of oral history interviews. When transcribing, flag the original spelling with "[sic]" only if the context requires it; otherwise leave as written.

1.2. "Shophouse" (one word) is standard for the traditional terrace commercial-residential building type. The two-word form "shop house" is deprecated. In captions and map labels, the one-word form is to be used consistently.

1.3. The term "Straits-born" (hyphenated, capital S) replaces "Straits Chinese" in all narrative sections. The older term may appear in quoted sources and in bibliographic entries where it forms part of a title. In index entries, cross-reference "Straits Chinese" to "Straits-born."

1.4. "Peranakan" is retained as a broader cultural descriptor and is not a synonym for "Straits-born." Use "Peranakan" only when referring to the wider community and its material culture; use "Straits-born" when the reference is specifically to the English-educated, Straits Settlements-born community.

1.5. The term "coolie" is no longer used in almanac prose, even in historical contexts. Replace with "labourer" or, where the historical record supports it, "indentured labourer." Do not silently alter quoted matter; add a bracketed editorial note, e.g., "[term used in the original]".

1.6. "Hokien" (common in older sources) is standardised to "Hokkien" in all almanac text, including map legends and list of abbreviations.

---

**2. Formatting of Dates and Numerals**

2.1. In running text, dates are written in the form "15 March 1892" (day, month, year — no comma between month and year). The all-numeral form "15/3/1892" is reserved for tables, database extracts, and citation strings.

2021 Style Update effective_date 2021-07-01 date. Record status: superseded.

2.2. When a date range spans two years, write "1887–1888" (en dash, no spaces). When the range is within the same year, write "March–April 1887". Do not use "from 1887-88" or "1887/88" in almanac text.

2.3. Decades are written as "the 1890s" (no apostrophe before the s). The apostrophe form "1890's" is not used except when quoting a source.

2.4. Approximate dates are written "c. 1875" (lowercase c, full stop, space). The abbreviation "ca." is no longer used. In genealogical charts, "c." may be omitted if the chart legend states that undated entries are approximate.

2.5. Numerals: For numbers below 100, write in words in running text ("forty-two"), except when the number is part of a date, a measurement, a table, or a person's age in a parenthetical note. Ages in parentheses are always numerals: "(aged 42)".

2.6. Large numbers: Use commas for thousands ("12,000") in running text and tables. Do not use spaces or full stops as thousand separators.

2.7. Measurements: Use metric units by default ("1.5 km", "3 m"). Imperial units may be given in parentheses after metric when the source uses them, but the metric value comes first. In direct quotations, retain the original units.

---

**3. Example Corrections and Illustrations**

3.1. The worked example in Section 7.4 of the 2019 Guidelines (the "Tan Kim Seng" family tree) contains an error in the birth order of the third generation. The corrected order is: (1) Tan Beng Swee, (2) Tan Beng Teck, (3) Tan Beng Huat, (4) Tan Beng Keong. The 2019 example incorrectly placed Tan Beng Teck third. This correction applies to all future reprints and to the online version.

documents.content:
**2021 Style Update for the Straits Ancestry Almanac**

**Amendment List — Issue 3 (1 July 2021)**

---

**4. Names and Name Ordering**

4.1. For Chinese names in the Straits Settlements, the historical record is mixed. In the 19th and early 20th centuries, the same individual may appear in English-language sources as "Tan Beng Swee" (surname first, as in Chinese convention) and in other records as "Beng Swee Tan" (surname last, following English convention). The almanac standard is as follows:

- **Primary entry:** Use the name form that is most common in the primary sources for that individual. For most Chinese residents of Singapore and Penang before 1942, this will be the surname-first form.
- **Cross-reference:** When an individual is known to have used both forms, include the alternative form in parentheses at first mention. Example: "Tan Beng Swee (Beng Swee Tan)".
- **Do not** silently convert one form to the other. If a source is ambiguous about which part is the surname, flag the entry with a footnote rather than guessing.

4.2. For Malay and Javanese names, do not assume that the last element is a surname. Use the full name as given in the source, and do not alphabetise by the final element unless the source itself does so. For example, "Mohamed Eusoff bin Abdullah" is alphabetised under "Mohamed", not "Abdullah". If a bin/binti patronymic is present, retain it in full.

4.3. For Tamil and other South Indian names, the convention varies. The almanac follows the source for the primary entry, but where a person is commonly known by an initial plus given name (e.g., "A. V. Pillay"), the entry is alphabetised under the initial. Do not expand initials unless the full name is confirmed by a second source.

4.4. Women's names: Where a woman is recorded under her married name in the primary sources, use that as the primary entry, with the maiden name in parentheses if known. Example: "Lim Choo Neo (née Lim Cheng Neo)". Do not use the "née" form for men.

4.5. Honorifics and titles (e.g., "Kapitan China", "Dato", "Sir", "Hajji") are not part of the name for alphabetisation purposes. They may be included in the entry text, but the sort key must ignore them. For example, "Kapitan China Tan Ah Hun" is alphabetised under "Tan".

4.6. When the same person appears under two different romanisations in different sources (e.g., "Wee" and "Ooi" for the same Hokkien surname), choose the spelling that appears in the earliest reliable record for that individual, and note the alternative spelling in the cross-reference. Do not standardise across individuals; each entry is decided on its own evidence.

---

**5. Additional Date and Place Conventions**

5.1. For dates that are known only by the year, write just the year (e.g., "1887"). Do not add "c." to a year that is certain. The "c." marker is only for dates that are approximate or uncertain.

5.2. For dates that are known to a month but not a day, write "March 1887" (no day, no comma). For dates known to a season or a festival, write "during Chinese New Year 1892" or "after Hari Raya Puasa 1901" — do not attempt to convert these to a specific calendar date.

5.3. For dates in the Chinese calendar or the Islamic (Hijri) calendar, give the conversion to the Gregorian calendar in brackets. Example: "the 15th day of the 8th lunar month [mid-September 1892]". The conversion should be marked as approximate if the exact Gregorian day is not determinable.

documents.content:
**Chapter 1. Purpose and Authority**

1.1 The Straits Ancestry Almanac is a quarterly publication, with a cumulative annual index issued each December. The Almanac records family histories, biographical sketches, and transcriptions of primary documents relevant to the genealogical study of families connected to Singapore, Malacca, Penang, and the wider region.

1.2 This manual is the sole governing instruction for all production and editorial decisions. It is issued by the Editorial Review Board, which holds final authority over content, format, and procedure.

1.3 The manual is effective from 15 January 2023. All work commenced on or after that date shall conform to these rules. Work in progress at the effective date shall be brought into conformity as soon as practicable, and in any event before the final proof stage of the relevant issue.

1.4 The manual is a controlled document. Copies are distributed in printed form to each department head and are maintained in the shared drive under the folder `PM2023`. The digital copy is the authoritative version. Printed copies are for convenience only and may become outdated.

1.5 The Editorial Review Board may issue amendments from time to time. Amendments shall be numbered sequentially and appended to this manual. No amendment shall take effect until it has been approved by the Board and recorded in the amendment log in Chapter 8.

1.6 In the event of any conflict between this manual and any other instruction—whether written, verbal, or electronic—this manual shall prevail. Departmental editors are responsible for bringing any such conflict to the attention of the Board.

---

2023 Production Manual effective_date 2023-01-15 date. Record status: current.

**Chapter 2. Version Control and the Governing Nature of This Manual**

2.1 The Almanac has, over the years, accumulated a large body of instructions: style sheets, editorial memos, checklists for transcribers, and notes from production meetings. Many of these were useful in their time but were never systematically reconciled. The result has been confusion, and occasionally error, when two instructions pointed in different directions.

2.2 This manual is the response to that confusion. It is the single point of reference for all production matters. It does not merely repeat earlier instructions; it supersedes them. Where an earlier instruction is silent on a matter, this manual supplies the rule. Where an earlier instruction is explicit but inconsistent with this manual, the earlier instruction is void.

2.3 The following documents are formally superseded by this manual:

- *Style Sheet for Transcribers, Rev. 4* (2018)
- *Editorial Memo 2019-02: Place-Name Conventions*
- *Editorial Memo 2020-07: Dating Conventions for Lunar Calendar Entries*
- *Checklist for Proofreaders, Rev. 2* (2021)
- *Workflow Diagram for Quarterly Issues* (2022)
- Any departmental notes, handwritten or typed, that conflict with the rules below

This list is not exhaustive. If a staff member is in doubt whether a particular instruction is still valid, the instruction should be treated as superseded unless it is consistent with this manual.

2.4 The manual is organised into chapters, each covering a distinct area of production. The chapters are intended to be read together. A rule in one chapter may qualify a rule in another; the cross-references are given where relevant.

2.5 The governing nature of this manual is not a formality. In past issues, errors have reached print because a transcriber followed an old note rather than the current rule. To prevent this, every department head shall, within one month of the effective date, review the instructions held by their staff and confirm in writing to the Board that the instructions have been reconciled with this manual.

**5.2 Publication status.** The Straits Ancestry Almanac publication_status in_production. Record status: current. For the avoidance of doubt, "in production" means that the editorial content has been finalised at the level of the volume editor, that the text has been copy-edited, and that the work is now in the hands of the design and typesetting team. It does not mean that the Almanac has been printed, nor that it has been released for sale. The publication date remains as announced in the Board's circular of 10 January 2023: 20 April 2023.

| Status | Effective from | Effective to | Remarks |
|---|---|---|---|
| In preparation | 1 June 2022 | 30 September 2022 | Initial compilation of genealogical returns from district offices. |

The entry "In review" recorded in the Board circular of 4 November 2022 is superseded by the current entry in 5.2. Any staff member relying on the November circular for the current status should disregard it for that purpose.

**5.4 Workflow from draft to production.** The following sequence describes the normal path for a chapter of the Almanac from draft to the production stage. It is the governing sequence for all chapters in the 2023 edition.

1. The volume editor submits a chapter draft to the Secretariat.
2. The Secretariat logs the draft in the tracking sheet `ALMANAC_TRACKING_2023.xlsx` and assigns a chapter number.
3. The draft is circulated to two internal readers, one from the Archives Division and one from the Publications Division.
4. The readers return their comments within ten working days. Comments are recorded on the copy of the draft, not on a separate sheet.
5. The volume editor revises the draft and returns it to the Secretariat.
6. The Secretariat sends the revised draft to the copy editor.
7. The copy editor returns the marked-up copy to the Secretariat, who then returns it to the volume editor for final approval.
8. Upon the volume editor's approval, the chapter is declared "final" in the tracking sheet.
9. The Secretariat forwards the final text to the design team, who prepare the typeset pages. At this point, the chapter is "in production."

Chapters that have reached step 9 are listed in the tracking sheet with the status "in production." The Board's status for the whole Almanac is independent of the status of individual chapters; a chapter may be in production while the Almanac as a whole is still recorded as in review, and vice versa.

**5.5 The tracking sheet.** The master copy of `ALMANAC_TRACKING_2023.xlsx` is held on the shared drive under `ALMANAC_2023`. No other copy of the tracking sheet is authoritative. Staff who update the tracking sheet shall do so on the shared drive copy only and shall not keep personal copies for longer than one working day.

**6.6 Approval of revisions.** This section governs all revisions to the 2023 edition, whether to the text, the cover, or the production specifications. It applies to revisions proposed at any stage, from the first draft of the text to the final PDF. The provisions of this section supersede any earlier practice of approving revisions by the Publications Division alone.

**6.6.1 Categories of revision.** For the purposes of this manual, a revision is classified as either:

- (a) a *minor revision*, being a change that does not alter the substance of the text or the visual appearance of the cover to a material degree. Examples include the correction of a typographical error, the adjustment of a caption to fit the page, and the substitution of one photograph of the same subject for another.
- (b) a *major revision*, being any other revision. Examples include the addition or removal of a family entry, the rewriting of a biographical note, the reordering of chapters, and any change to the cover design or the binding specifications.

The classification of a revision as minor or major shall be made by the Publications Division. If the Publications Division is in doubt, the revision shall be treated as major.

**6.6.2 Approval required for major revisions.** Editorial Review Board approval_required major_revisions. Record status: current. This is the standing instruction of the Board, confirmed at its meeting of 15 January 2023, and it remains in force until the Board resolves otherwise. No major revision may be incorporated into the text, the cover, or the production specifications unless the Board has approved it in the manner set out in section 6.6.3.

Minor revisions do not require the approval of the Board. They shall be recorded by the Publications Division in the revision log described in section 6.6.5.

**6.6.3 Procedure for seeking approval of a major revision.** The following procedure shall be followed for every major revision:

1. The person proposing the revision (the proposer) shall submit a written request to the Publications Division. The request shall describe the proposed revision, state the reason for it, and identify the page or section of the almanac affected. The request may be sent by email to the Publications Division mailbox (publications@straitsancestry.org.sg), marked "MAJOR REVISION – 2023 ALMANAC" in the subject line.
2. The Publications Division shall review the request within two working days. If the request is incomplete, the Division shall return it to the proposer with a note of the missing information.
3. If the Publications Division agrees that the request is a major revision, it shall prepare a revision note in the standard format (Form SAA-RM-01, available from the Secretariat). The revision note shall summarise the proposed revision, its effect on the text or cover, and any cost or schedule implications.
4. The revision note shall be circulated to the Board by the Secretariat at least five working days before the Board meeting at which it is to be considered. The circulation shall be by email, with the revision note attached as a PDF.
5. The Board shall consider the revision note at its next ordinary meeting, or at a special meeting convened for the purpose. The Board may approve the revision, approve it with conditions, or reject it. The decision of the Board shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting.
6. The Secretariat shall inform the proposer and the Publications Division of the Board's decision within two working days of the meeting. The decision shall be confirmed in writing by email.

**6.6.4 Handling of conflicting revisions.** From time to time, two or more revision requests
may touch the same page, table, or index entry, or a revision may be proposed while an earlier
revision of the same material is still under review. The following rules shall govern in every such
case.

1.  Where two revision requests are received on the same working day and both affect the same
    page or entry, the Publications Division shall log them in the order in which they arrived,
    by timestamp of the email or, for requests delivered by hand, by the time of receipt at the
    Secretariat. The earlier request shall be deemed the governing revision for the purpose of
    the 2023 almanac. The later request shall be processed as a further revision and shall not
    override the earlier one unless the Board expressly decides otherwise.
2.  Where a revision request conflicts with a revision that was approved before 1 January 2023
    but has not yet been implemented in the working text, the Publications Division shall bring
    the conflict to the attention of the Board at its next meeting. Pending the Board's decision,
    the working text shall carry both proposed versions, each marked with a note in the margin
    reading "CONFLICT – see revision log entry [number]".
3.  Where a revision request conflicts with a revision that has already been implemented in the
    printed 2022 almanac, the 2022 text shall stand unless the Board approves a change. The
    proposer shall be informed that the request will be treated as a new revision, not a
    correction of an error.
4.  If a revision request is found to conflict with a provision of this manual, or with the
    Straits Ancestry Society's constitution, the manual or the constitution, as the case may be,
    shall govern. The Publications Division shall note the conflict on the revision request and
    return it to the proposer with an explanation. The proposer may resubmit the request in a

**6.6.5 Revision log.** The Publications Division shall maintain a revision log for the 2023
almanac in the form of a spreadsheet, kept on the shared drive at

- the section, page, or entry affected;
- a one-line summary of the revision;

placed before the Board at each ordinary meeting.

**7 Field Research and Branch Office Integration**

**7.1 Purpose of this chapter.** This chapter sets out the procedures for field researchers
working on the 2023 almanac, and the manner in which material gathered in the field, or
submitted by branch offices, shall be incorporated into the working text. It supplements the
general provisions of Chapter 3 (Sources and Citations) and Chapter 6 (Editorial Workflow).
Where any provision in this chapter conflicts with a provision in Chapter 3 or Chapter 6, the
provision in the earlier chapter shall govern.

**7.2 Field researcher checklists.** Every field researcher shall complete, for each field trip,
the checklist at Form SAA-FR-01 (Field Trip Checklist) and, for each separate item of
research, the checklist at Form SAA-FR-02 (Research Item Checklist). The checklists are
reproduced at Annex D and Annex E respectively. A condensed version of the principal
requirements is set out below for quick reference. This condensed version is a convenience
only; it does not alter the requirements of the forms.

*Pre-departure (Form SAA-FR-01, Part A):*

- Confirm the research itinerary with the Research & Archives Division at least five working
  days before departure.
- Obtain from the Division a copy of the current research brief for the relevant chapter or
  entry.
- Check that the digital recorder, camera, and portable scanner are in working order, and
  that spare batteries and memory cards are packed.
- Carry at least two printed copies of the consent form (Form SAA-C-01) and the
  interviewee information sheet.
- Notify the Division of the expected return date and the contact number for the field
  location.

*In the field (Form SAA-FR-01, Part B):*

- Record the date and place of each visit in the field notebook at the time of the visit.
- Photograph the exterior and, where permitted, the interior of each building or site
  visited, and note the photograph numbers against the relevant entry in the notebook.
- Where a document is examined but not copied, record the repository, the reference
  number, and a summary of the contents sufficient to identify the document.
- Where a document is copied, record the repository and reference number on the copy
  itself, in pencil, before the copy is placed in the research file.
- Note the names and designations of all persons spoken to, and the date of each
  conversation.

*On return (Form SAA-FR-01, Part C):*

- Submit the field notebook, photographs, and copies to the Research & Archives Division
  within five working days of return.
- Complete the expense claim within ten working days of return.
- File the completed checklist with the Division.

**7.3 Research item checklist.** For each separate item of research — that is, each distinct
fact, document, or record sought — the researcher shall complete a Research Item Checklist
(Form SAA-FR-02). The purpose of this form is to record, for the benefit of the editorial
staff, the status of the item and the location of any supporting material. The form shall
contain the following fields:

- Item number (in the form FR-2023-001, FR-2023-002, and so on);
- the chapter and entry to which the item relates;
- a description of the item sought;
- the repository or repositories searched;
- the outcome (found, not found, or partially found);
- where found, the repository, reference, and shelf or box number;
- the location of any copy made (research file number and page);
- the date the item was sought; and
- the name of the researcher.

documents.content:
**Appendix A: Citation Formats**

All citations in the Almanac, whether in the text, the endnotes, or the bibliography, shall follow the formats set out below. The Editorial Review Board has adopted these formats to ensure that every source can be traced by a reader or by a later researcher without recourse to the originating office. Researchers and editors shall not devise their own variants.

**A.1 Archival documents.** For documents held in a repository, cite the repository name, the fonds or collection title, the series and file reference, and the date of the document. Where the document is a letter, include the writer and recipient if known.

Example (endnote form):

> National Archives of Singapore, Straits Settlements Records, Series R4, File 12/1887, "Letter from the Resident Councillor, Malacca, to the Colonial Secretary, 14 June 1887."

For documents from a private family collection, cite the name of the collection and the item number assigned by the Division, e.g.:

> Tan Kim Seng Family Papers, private collection, item TKS-2019-014, "Receipt for the purchase of land at Telok Ayer, 3 March 1852."

**A.2 Published works.** For books, cite author, title, edition (if not the first), place of publication, publisher, year, and page. For journal articles, cite author, article title, journal title, volume, issue, year, and page.

**A.3 Newspapers.** Cite the newspaper title, date, page, and column. Where the article is unsigned, the title of the article stands in place of the author.

**A.4 Oral history interviews.** Cite the name of the interviewee, the interviewer, the date of the interview, the repository holding the recording, and the accession number. Where a transcript is used, cite the transcript page.

Example:

> Interview with Mdm Lim Guat Neo, by the Division, 12 August 2023, National Archives of Singapore, Oral History Centre, Accession No. 004812, transcript p. 3.

**A.5 Photographs and maps.** Cite the photographer or cartographer if known, the title or description, the date, the repository, and the reference number. For photographs taken by Division staff, cite the photograph number as recorded in the field notebook (see Section 7.2).

**Appendix B: Glossary of Terms**

The following terms are used throughout this Manual and in the working papers of the Almanac. The definitions are the working definitions adopted by the Editorial Review Board and shall govern unless a contrary meaning is plainly intended.

**Ancestral tablet.** A wooden or stone tablet inscribed with the names of deceased family members, commonly found in clan houses and family shrines. For the purposes of the Almanac, a tablet is treated as a primary source only where its inscription can be dated or corroborated.

**Batu.** A stone marker, often a grave marker or a boundary stone. The term appears in field notes and in place names.

**Congregation.** A body of persons gathered for religious worship. In the context of the Almanac, the term is used in the records of churches and temples.

**Fonds.** The whole of the records created or accumulated by a person, family, or corporate body in the course of that body's activities. The term is used in archival description.
